objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus compression feedback system in reducing tissue compression before staple deployment
controls: Historical average tissue compression (3.5 mm) before staple deployment
Average tissue compression ≥ 3.5 mm before staple deployment in 8 out of 10 patients
baseline: Historical average tissue compression (3.5 mm) before staple deployment
procedure: Recruit 20 patients with varying tissue types and staple deployment pressures
Deploy staples with and without the Nucleus compression feedback system activated
Measure tissue compression before staple deployment in all patients
Collect data on tissue type, staple deployment pressure, and Nucleus compression feedback system activation status
expected_result: Tissue compression (mm) before staple deployment will decrease by 1.2 mm when the Nucleus compression feedback system is activated
falsification_condition: Average tissue compression ≥ 3.5 mm before staple deployment in 8 out of 10 patients
sample_requirements: 20 patients with varying tissue types and staple deployment pressures
safety_constraints: Ensure that the Nucleus compression feedback system does not cause any adverse effects on the patients
information_gain: The effectiveness of the Nucleus compression feedback system in reducing tissue compression before staple deployment, and the potential for improving surgical outcomes
